newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends slightly lower as rally unravels.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends slightly lower as rally unravels.

text.p: U.S. blue chips ended lower on Tuesday after a wild ride in which a 100-point gain in the Dow Jones Industrial Average unraveled in the last hours of the session.
The late sell-off left the Dow down five points for an unofficial close of 6656. The average has now fallen for five straight sessions, the first time is has done so since last June.
The volatile session mirrored one in the bond market, where a rally also lost steam late in the day.
Stocks and bonds had surged after the morning release of the closely watched employment cost index (ECI), which showed U.S. labor costs were not rising quite as fast as investors had thought.
"The ECI started the day off well and said there is no current danger of inflation even with the unemployment rate as low as it is," said Stan Shipley, senior strategist at Lehman Brothers.
Later, however, strong retail sales and consumer confidence data led to an erosion of the bond market's advance and triggered profit-taking in stocks.

"The ECI was a good excuse for a bounce, and there was a lot of short-covering going on early," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "But when people saw the market up 100 points and yields starting to work back up toward seven percent, the bounce got sold."
Analysts said the market's failure to hold its gains indicated further headway was unlikely soon.
"I read it as an indication of subsiding momentum," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst at Janney, Montgomery Scott. "We expect the market will probably show some expansive swings here."
Some issues were able to sidestep the general retreat. A particularly notable example was International Business Machines Corp, which broke a four-session losing streak by jumping 4-1/4 to 150-3/4.
IBM declared a two-for-one stock split and benefited from a upgrade by Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones, who now rates the company a strong buy.
Drug shares were strong after several companies reported better-than-expected earnings. Merck and Co Inc climbed 2-1/2 to 87, and Eli Lilly and Co, which reported on Monday, gained 1-7/8 to 82-1/4.

ITT Corp soared 14-1/8 to 56-3/4 in the first trading since the company received a $55-per-share hostile bid from Hilton Hotels Corp. Analysts said Hilton would probably have to raise its offer to complete the deal.

Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) climbed 1-3/4 to 38-3/4. The company, which is the nation's largest source of funds for home mortgages, said it exceeded all of its housing goals set by regulators in 1996.
The S&P 500 index closed unchanged at 765.02.
The Nasdaq Composite closed at 1354.37, for a 1.56 point rise. Early in the session, the index reached as high as 1370.
3Com Corp was Nasdaq's most active issue, falling 3-1/2 to 61-1/4 after climbing as high as 68-3/4.
